text:
The user wants to compare two score files from a direct model run: Map A (F4/emsr279-11_s1_pre.json) covers 2017-09-14/2017-09-15, and Map B (F4/emsr279-11_s1_post.json) covers 2018-04-19. They're asking "where do they differ, and which one is correct?"

I should use olmoearth_compare_review with scores_path_a, scores_path_b, date_a, and date_b. The file names are given as relative paths ("F4/emsr279-11_s1_pre.json"). The tool expects .json files under OLMOEARTH_SCORES_ROOT. I can pass the given paths as-is and check whether they exist. If not, an error will be returned, so at that point I'll adjust.

Important caveat: without ground truth labels, we cannot say which map is correct — this must be explicitly stated. According to the tool's description, "which side is correct" cannot be resolved without labels, so it must be declined with reasons. Also, since dates differ, the differences could represent actual changes over time, and a 'dates' block would be output for that purpose.

Since there is no grid information for boundary interpretation, I might omit grid. Let me call olmoearth_compare_review with the following arguments:
- scores_path_a: F4/emsr279-11_s1_pre.json
- scores_path_b: F4/emsr279-11_s1_post.json
- date_a: 2017-09-14/2017-09-15
- date_b: 2018-04-19
- max_listed default

These are direct files (score files), so no need to go through olmoearth_scores_from_file first. That tool is for reading a scores raster + manifest.json directory. Here, the user has provided .json files directly, and according to the tool description, compare_review accepts them ("scores inline, or as .json files under OLMOEARTH_SCORES_ROOT").

Let's make the call.

result.which_side_is_right: not graded: the maps describe different times, so a window where they differ may have changed on the ground; no labels_date was given, so no grading is possible even with labels
result.evidence_scope: On 15 pairs of Sen1Floods11 flood maps with expert labels (exp58: window level; crop offsets, backbones, sensors, fine-tuning and encoders) the more confident side was right on 51 to 70 percent of differing windows, which does not cover this pair: no recorded experiment grades which of these two maps is right, and without labels neither side can be picked.
must_state: No recorded experiment grades which of these two maps is right; without labels neither side can be picked.
The maps describe different times, so where they differ the ground may have changed; a difference is not by itself an error.
result.class_pairs_reading: class_pairs counts, for each unordered pair of classes, the windows where one map has one class and the other map the other, both directions together; 'directions' splits that count by which map has which class, as class_changes does.
result.listing_order: the 10 listed windows are the first differing windows in window order (from row 0), not a sample of them; all 1,570 are in the file at differing_path, in the same order. Read which classes change, in which direction and where from class_changes, class_pairs, spatial and facts, not from the list

spatial.reading: Each band is a strip of whole rows (row_bands) or whole columns (col_bands) of the window grid, numbered from 0: row band 0 holds row 0, the grid's top (the north edge of a north-up map), and column band 0 holds column 0. share_of_differing is the band's share of ALL differing windows; share_of_windows is its share of all compared windows, the share an even spread would give it; share_of_band_differing is the share of the band's own windows that differ. top_band_share is row band 0's share_of_differing; max_band is the band, of either axis, holding the most differing windows.

facts.sentence: The most common change is class 0 (not water) in map A to class 1 (water) in map B: 1,247 of the 1,570 differing windows (79.4%); the reverse, class 1 (water) in map A to class 0 (not water) in map B, is 323 (20.6%).

Map A has the larger margin on 77.6% of the 1,570 differing windows (map B on 22.4%); this does not make A right there: upstream the more confident side was right on 51 to 70 percent of differing windows (exp58).

Of the 1,570 differing windows, 1.6% lie in the northmost row band (rows 0-1399, band 0 of 4), which holds 24.8% of all compared windows; the most in any band, 46.8%, lie in rows 2800-4199 (50-75% of the grid's 5,600 rows, band 2), which holds 25.1% of all compared windows.

forbidden_claims.why: the maps describe different or overlapping periods (2017-09-14/2017-09-15 and 2018-04-19): a window where they differ either changed on the ground or is wrong in one map, and another unlabelled map, of any date, cannot tell which; only a reference dated to each map can
no labels were used: nothing here says which map is right, more accurate or better; neither map is shown right where they differ, and the more confident side is not thereby the right one

dates.reading: the maps describe 2017-09-14/2017-09-15 and 2018-04-19, periods 216 days apart (their starts 217 days apart): a window where they differ either changed on the ground between them (seasonal cycles included) or is wrong in one map, and the decisions alone cannot say which; a reference for each date separates the two

content:
Compared all 78,028 shared windows; **1,570 differ (2.0%)**. Full list of differing windows: `.../workspace/compare_differing_eec2555155.json`

**Direction of change**

| A (2017-09) | B (2018-04) | Windows | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| not water | water | 1,247 | 79.4% |
| water | not water | 323 | 20.6% |

Net direction: mostly drier-to-flooded between the two dates.

**Where they concentrate**: most differing windows are in rows 2,800–4,199 (mid-south of the grid, 46.8%); the north band has the fewest (1.6%). Changes are spread fairly evenly across columns.

**Confidence**: map A holds the larger margin on 77.6% of differing windows (mean margin A 0.389 vs B 0.158). That does not make A right — upstream evidence says the more-confident side was correct on only 51–70% of differing windows, and that record does not cover this pair.

**Which is right? Neither can be.** The maps are 216 days apart, so any difference may be real ground change rather than an error; without labels dated to each map, no one side can be picked. To settle it you'd need references for both dates (a label set per period, then re-run with `labels_date`).
